memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Priests must not shave their heads or shave off the edges of their
beards or cut their bodies'" - Lev 21:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These may sound like odd rules about grooming, but they were not about
fashion. The surrounding nations expressed grief for the dead by
shaving their heads, gashing their skin and cutting their bodies.
Often these acts were tied to pagan worship and attempts to appease
the spirits of the dead.

God was drawing a clear line. His priests would not mourn like people
who had no hope and no living God. They would grieve, yes, but not in
ways that copied the religions around them.

Every generation faces this same question in some form. The world has
its own ways of handling pain, fear and loss. Some of those ways are
harmless. Some quietly pull the heart away from God. The believer must
learn to tell the difference.

Dear friend, the pressure to blend in is real. Paul wrote that we
should not be conformed to the pattern of this world but transformed
by the renewing of our minds (Rom 12:2). That transformation is not
about becoming strange or unfriendly. It is about being shaped by
truth rather than by the crowd.

When sorrow comes, where do you run? To numbing habits, or to the God
who holds you? Christ has given us a better way to carry pain.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I quietly copying the world's ways of handling pain?
2. What habits do I turn to first when I am hurting?
3. How can God's Word reshape my response to sorrow this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, keep me from drifting into the patterns of the world without
noticing. Renew my mind and teach me to bring my sorrow straight to
You. Amen.
